jobs.prompt:
ci(cpp): build downloadable ARM64 release packages of the native gateway for Linux and macOS

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-pi-compat-20261118-44214118327-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: a known-good state of `cpp/gateway/`, a C++20 port of this repository's TypeScript gateway (`src/`, `serve.ts`), with a JavaScript-style runtime layer (`include/uos/rt`, `src/rt`, `src/runtime`), vendored simdjson and simdutf (`cpp/gateway/third_party/`), ICU for Unicode, and about 442 standalone test binaries (`cpp/gateway/tests/**/*_test.cpp`). On this state the release build passes its whole suite on Linux ARM64. The native gateway is already 1.2-1.9x faster than the TypeScript gateway on Bun end to end and uses about a third of the memory (`cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-perf-request-path-20261117.md`). Every deployment target is 64-bit ARM: an Arch Linux ARM VPS, an Apple Silicon Mac and a Raspberry Pi.

OWNER POLICY (binding): generic functionality comes from mature open-source or standard libraries; exact parity with Bun's quirks and error wording is NOT required; less first-party code is preferred. What must hold: the gateway's functional behaviour (wire formats, status codes, stored data, authentication and validation decisions, accounting) and security never getting weaker.

READ FIRST: `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (portable build-and-test driver; invoke it as `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh ...`, the file lacks its executable bit), `cpp/gateway/docs/BUILD.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/RUNTIME.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/OSS-REPLACEMENT-PLAN.md`, `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md` (its coroutine rules are mandatory; its "Host safety" and "compile only through tools/unit.sh" rules apply to the authors' server, not to your disposable runner; where it demands exact Bun parity, the owner policy above wins). `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py <test>` prints a test's application sources; every `src/rt/*.cpp` and the vendored libraries link into every test.

About ten other agents are changing other parts of `cpp/gateway` on their own branches at the same time (URL, HTTP parsing, regex, WebSocket, passkey CBOR and ASN.1, BigInt, date/console/filesystem/env/headers helpers, the stored-value reader, a test-suite repair). Your branch will be merged with theirs: stay strictly inside your OWNED PATHS and keep everything else byte-identical.

GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- Do not edit `.github/` (unless your task says so), the TypeScript, or `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`. Do not delete or weaken tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive in a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 as `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` describes. Bun 1.4.0 may be installed when you need to run the TypeScript.

OWNED PATHS (you may create or edit only these, plus your report)
- `.github/workflows/cpp-gateway-release.yml` (new), `cpp/gateway/packaging/**`, `cpp/gateway/docs/RELEASES.md` (new)

TASK
The owner needs installable artefacts for three machines: an Arch Linux ARM VPS, a Raspberry Pi (Raspberry Pi OS, glibc 2.36+), and an Apple Silicon Mac. This branch already has a verified recipe for a PORTABLE Linux ARM64 package (`cpp/gateway/packaging/portable/`, guide `cpp/gateway/docs/RASPBERRY-PI.md`, report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-pi-compat-20261118.md`: built in a Debian 12 arm64 container, only glibc 2.36 required, proven in Debian 12 and 13 containers) and a macOS build script (`cpp/gateway/tools/macos-build.sh`, `cpp/gateway/docs/MACOS.md`). Turn them into a release pipeline: a workflow, triggered by `workflow_dispatch` and by pushing a tag matching `cpp-gateway-v*`, with two jobs: (1) on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, run the portable build, run its container proofs (Debian 12 and 13), and upload `uos-gateway-linux-arm64.tar.gz` plus a `SHA256SUMS` file and the proof log as artefacts; (2) on `macos-latest` (Apple Silicon), build the gateway with the macOS script, run the runtime test gate the script already defines, package the gateway and its tools with the licences, and upload `uos-gateway-macos-arm64.tar.gz` plus `SHA256SUMS`. Each tarball contains the gateway executable, the KV tools, the licences of every statically linked library, a `VERSION` file (commit, build date from the commit timestamp so the build is reproducible, compiler and library versions) and a short `INSTALL.md`. The workflow has `permissions: contents: read`, `persist-credentials: false`, no secrets, pinned action versions as used by the existing `cpp-gateway-*.yml` workflows, and does NOT create a GitHub release or push anything (the owner downloads the artefacts). Make the packaging scripts runnable locally with one documented command each, and reproducible: building the same commit twice on your runner must give byte-identical tarballs (fix timestamps, ordering and owner/group in the archive). Write `docs/RELEASES.md` for a non-expert: how to trigger the workflow, where to download, how to verify the checksum, how to install on each of the three machines, and how to roll back. You are on Linux: you cannot run the macOS job; make it as correct as you can from `MACOS.md` and the script, validate the workflow with `actionlint`, and say plainly in the report that the macOS job is unexecuted.

DONE WHEN
The Linux package builds twice to identical bytes on your ARM64 runner and passes both container proofs through the same commands the workflow uses, `actionlint` passes, and `docs/RELEASES.md` is complete.
